title: Bring it on now, they said, mocking the Day of Account.
subtitle: Asking for consequences as a joke
then: The idolaters asked Allah to {trap}hasten their share before the Day of Reckoning{/trap}. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said they were asking for the punishment to come early. Ibn Jarir said they asked for whatever they deserved, good or bad, right now. Ibn Kathir says they said it in mockery.
now: Someone reminds you about the Day of Account and you laugh it off: if it is real, let it come. {trap}A joke can be a way of not thinking.{/trap} {idea}The delay is not proof it is false. It is time given to you.{/idea}
old: If consequences were real, they would have come already.
new: The delay is mercy and time, not evidence that nothing is coming.
try: Notice one serious thing you usually joke about. Sit with it quietly for a minute instead.

title: Be patient with their words, and remember Dawud, who kept returning.
subtitle: Strength that turns back to Allah again and again
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to be patient and to remember Dawud. Ibn Kathir explains his strength as {idea}strength in knowledge, action and obedience{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved prayer and fasting to Allah were those of Dawud, and that {reward}he always turned to Allah{/reward}.
now: Your manager's comment stings all afternoon. You could replay it on the drive home, or you could do what Dawud did: {idea}turn back to Allah, again{/idea}. Not once. Every time.
old: Being strong means not needing anyone.
new: Real strength keeps turning back to Allah, in every matter, again and again.
try: The next time someone's words hurt today, pause and say Astaghfirullah before you reply.

title: The mountains praised Allah with him, morning and evening.
subtitle: When your remembrance joins all of creation
then: Allah made {idea}the mountains glorify His praise with Dawud{/idea} at sunrise and at the end of the day. Ibn Kathir says the lofty mountains would echo his glorification. Ibn Abbas understood Salat Ad-Duha from the words ishraq, the time after sunrise.
now: Early morning, before the house wakes. You say SubhanAllah by the kitchen window and it feels small. {idea}It is not small.{/idea} The hills on the horizon are saying it too.
old: My little dhikr in the morning hardly counts for anything.
new: When I glorify Allah, I join something that mountains are part of.
try: Tomorrow after sunrise, say SubhanAllah ten times while looking at something in nature.

title: Even the birds gathered and joined his praise.
subtitle: A sincere voice draws others in
then: Ibn Kathir says if a bird flew by Dawud and heard him reciting the Zabur, {idea}it would not go away{/idea}. It stayed hovering in the air, glorifying Allah with him. All of them followed him in praise.
now: Your child hears you reciting softly after Fajr and comes to sit beside you without being asked. {reward}No lecture did that.{/reward} Sincere worship has its own pull.
old: To bring others to good, I have to push and convince them.
new: Sincere worship draws others in more than any argument can.
try: Recite a short surah aloud at home today where your family can hear, gently.

title: A strong kingdom, wisdom, and clear judgement in speech.
subtitle: The gifts that made Dawud a just ruler
then: Allah made Dawud's kingdom strong. Mujahid said he was the most powerful of the people of the world. He was also given {idea}wisdom and sound judgement{/idea}, which Mujahid explained as soundness in speech and in deciding cases. Ibn Kathir says this became a basis of judging in this Ummah.
now: You are the oldest sibling, and your word settles arguments at home. Or you lead a small team. {idea}Authority is a gift that needs wisdom{/idea}, and the wisdom to speak clearly and fairly.
old: Having authority means my opinion wins.
new: Any authority I have is a gift from Allah that comes with a duty to judge fairly.
try: In one disagreement today, hear both sides fully before you decide anything.

title: Two disputants climbed the wall into his private chamber.
subtitle: A test that came without warning
then: Ibn Kathir says many stories told about this passage come from {trap}Isra'iliyat narrations{/trap}, with nothing authentic from the Prophet ﷺ. So {idea}it is better to speak briefly and leave its knowledge to Allah{/idea}. Dawud was in his mihrab, the noblest part of his house, where no one was to enter that day.
now: A forwarded message tells a dramatic story about a prophet, full of details you have never seen. {idea}The Quran's own words are enough.{/idea} You do not need to fill the gaps with rumours.
old: The more detail a story has, the more I understand it.
new: When the source is silent, I stay with what is true and leave the rest to Allah.
try: Before forwarding a religious story today, check where it comes from. If unsure, do not send it.

title: Do not fear: judge between us with truth.
subtitle: A frightened judge still asked to be fair
then: Dawud {trap}was terrified of them{/trap} because they came in where no one was supposed to enter. They told him not to fear. They were two litigants, one had wronged the other, and they asked him to {idea}judge with truth and not be unjust{/idea}.
now: Your phone rings late and it is two cousins, both shouting, both wanting you on their side. Your heart is racing. {idea}Breathe, then be fair.{/idea} Fear and anger make poor judges.
old: When I am caught off guard, I cannot be expected to be fair.
new: Even when startled, I can settle myself and give each side the truth.
try: When someone brings you a complaint today, ask the other side before you take a position.

title: Ninety-nine ewes, and he still wanted my one.
subtitle: When having more makes someone want everything
then: One of the two said his brother had {reward}ninety-nine ewes{/reward} while he had one. The brother said hand it over, and {trap}overpowered him in speech{/trap}, meaning he defeated him in argument.
now: The big supplier squeezes the small shop owner on price because they can. The sibling with the bigger house still wants the inheritance split their way. {trap}Winning the argument is not the same as being in the right.{/trap}
old: If I can argue it well, it must be fair.
new: Being better at talking does not make taking from someone right.
try: Think of one place you hold more power than someone. Ask if you are taking more than your share.

title: He judged the case, then realized he was the one tested.
subtitle: Dawud fell in prostration and turned back
then: Dawud said the brother had wronged him, and that many partners oppress one another, {idea}except those who believe and do good, and they are few{/idea}. Then he understood Allah had tested him, and {reward}fell prostrate in repentance{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ prostrated at this verse and said Dawud did it in repentance, and we do it in thanks.
now: You give your friend advice about being fair at work, and on the drive home you realize it applies to you. {reward}That moment is a gift.{/reward} Do not argue with it. Turn back.
old: When I see a fault, it is usually in someone else.
new: Sometimes the case I am judging is a mirror, and the right response is sajdah.
try: Make one sajdah today just to ask forgiveness for something you saw in yourself.

title: So We forgave him, and gave him nearness and a good return.
subtitle: Repentance that ends in closeness
then: Allah forgave him. Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Resurrection he will have {reward}nearness to Allah and the lofty levels of Paradise{/reward}, because of his repentance and his justice. He cites the hadith that those who are just with their families and those in their care will be on minbars of light.
now: You made a mistake you are ashamed of, and you think it has cancelled you. {reward}Repentance did not lower Dawud. It raised him.{/reward} The way back is also a way up.
old: After a serious mistake, I will always be less in Allah's sight.
new: Sincere repentance can bring me nearer to Allah than I was before.
try: Be fair to one person in your family or care today in a small, specific way.

title: Judge with truth and do not follow your desire.
subtitle: Advice to anyone given authority
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}advice to rulers and leaders{/idea}. A scholar once reminded a Khalifah: are you dearer to Allah than Dawud? Allah gave Dawud prophethood and rule, and still warned him {trap}not to follow desire{/trap}. As-Suddi said the punishment comes for what they neglected to do for the Day of Reckoning.
now: You are the parent deciding who gets the car, the manager writing reviews, the class rep. You like one person more. {trap}Desire whispers the answer before the facts arrive.{/trap} Remember who will review your decision.
old: My judgement is fair because I am a fair person.
new: Anyone can be pulled by desire, even a prophet was warned, so I check myself.
try: Before one decision today, ask: would I decide the same if I disliked this person?

title: None of this was created without purpose.
subtitle: The heavens and earth point to a return
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}did not create the creatures in vain{/idea}. He created them to worship Him, then He will gather them. The idea that nothing comes after this world is {trap}the assumption of those who disbelieve{/trap}.
now: A long week of deadlines, laundry, and traffic. At night you wonder if any of it means anything. {idea}It does.{/idea} Every ordinary day sits inside a purpose bigger than the to-do list.
old: Most of my days are just routine, with no real point.
new: Nothing was created aimlessly, including my ordinary days.
try: Tonight, name one routine task and make an intention to do it for Allah tomorrow.

title: Would Allah treat the doers of good like the corrupters?
subtitle: Justice needs another world
then: Ibn Kathir says we see {trap}evildoers prospering until they die{/trap}, and oppressed believers dying in grief. Allah does not do a speck of injustice, so {idea}there must be a time when the rights of the oppressed are restored{/idea}. If not here, then in another realm.
now: The colleague who cut corners got the promotion. The honest one was let go. You start to think honesty is for fools. {idea}The account is not closed yet.{/idea} Keep doing good.
old: If cheaters win and the honest lose, being good does not pay.
new: Allah will not treat the good and the corrupt the same. The final account is still ahead.
try: Do one honest thing today that costs you a little, trusting the account is with Allah.
